packages.title: Home: the calendar card says reminders come more and more often as the day gets closer; ‘Is TaskFlow free?’ says reminders are free, and Pro adds reminders in your own words
files: tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts:656 and :662-666 (the comment and `CALENDAR_BODY`), :759 (a test's title), :955-970 (WP59's ending test), and the acceptance tests (web-ux-tester)
brief: The owner answered WD20 and WD21 «yes» on 2026-10-22 (evening), WD21 against plan 1's «not now» (`.claude/ux-web/DECISIONS.md:7-11`, entry ‘2026-10-22 (evening) — WD20 and WD21 of run 2026-10-22-changes’). That makes two short additions on the home, in EN/ES/CA (`/`, `/es/`, `/ca/`): one clause on the calendar card (WEB-1103), and in the FAQ's ‘Is TaskFlow free?’ a sentence saying reminders are free plus a Pro clause for reminders asked for in your own words (WEB-1104). Only two values change in each of `src/content/site/{en,es,ca}.ts`. WP59 (plan 1, committed in 883d4d1) shortened the calendar sentence this package extends: start from what's on `dev`.

WEB-1103 (S2, WD20). The ‘Your day on one calendar’ / «Tu día en un calendario» / «El teu dia en un calendari» card ends ‘TaskFlow can remind you of tasks with a date.’ Since reminder plans (app aa2f53a, 2026-10-22), anyone, free or Pro, can have a task's reminders come more and more often as its day gets closer, worked out on the phone with no AI and no connection (`Backend/docs/REMINDER_PLANS.md:11, 50-56`; `.claude/ux-review/DECISIONS.md:15-24`). It's the owner's own reason for the feature (a project three weeks away), and the card never says it. Add review F's clause to the card's last sentence, in the words the owner approved. The paragraph (`features.calendar.body` at `src/content/site/en.ts:61`, `es.ts:61`, `ca.ts:61`) becomes: EN `See your tasks by day, week or month, beside the events from your phone’s calendars if you like. TaskFlow can remind you of tasks with a date, more and more often as the day gets closer.` / ES `Mira tus tareas por día, semana o mes, junto a los eventos de los calendarios del teléfono si quieres. TaskFlow puede recordarte las tareas con fecha, cada vez más a menudo según se acerca el día.` / CA `Mira les tasques per dia, setmana o mes, al costat dels esdeveniments dels calendaris del telèfon si vols. TaskFlow et pot recordar les tasques amb data, cada cop més sovint a mesura que s’acosta el dia.` Only the last full stop becomes a comma followed by the clause; the first sentence is unchanged. The English paragraph goes from 27 words to 36; the new last sentence is 18 words in English, 17 in Spanish and 18 in Catalan.

Why the clause is true, after D1–D7 too: the three strengths remind every 7, 3 or 2 days far from the day, then daily for the last days and on the day itself, for free and Pro alike (`REMINDER_PLANS.md:11, 50-56`). D2 starts them at most 4 weeks before the day, and D4 makes a task without a deadline count back from its own day, so ‘the day’ covers both the deadline and the task's day. ‘Can’ keeps it true where there's no plan: a repeating task (`:23`), a task given to someone else (D6, `:78`), a day less than 2 days away (`App/lib/widgets/reminder_plan_sheet.dart:462-464`), and reminders turned off in Settings (`REMINDER_PLANS.md:69`). The clause describes the app and quotes nothing. The app's line for a strength reads «Cada vez más a menudo hasta el jue 12» (`reminderPlanGrowing`; «cada cop més sovint» is its Catalan, in `App/lib/l10n/app_ca.arb`), but the site's clause has no quotation marks, label, number or date, so it stays true if the app's D1–D7 round renames anything. Don't add the strengths, the 4 weeks, the offer after saving, shared tasks or a rhythm said while dictating.

WEB-1104 (S1, WD21). The FAQ's second item, ‘Is TaskFlow free?’ / «¿TaskFlow es gratis?» / «TaskFlow és gratuït?», lists what Pro gives (unlimited dictation and file space, and typed sentences turned into tasks) but not reminders asked for in your own words. With Pro, a task's reminder sheet reads a rhythm you type or say, such as «cada 3 días y la última semana a diario», with Google's AI (`REMINDER_PLANS.md:13, 90-105`). Without Pro, that row shows a Pro badge, opens the Pro screen and sends nothing (`App/lib/widgets/reminder_plan_sheet.dart:571-579`). The owner wants it in the Pro list next to unlimited dictation and file space, and the free part must still say that the until-the-day reminders are for everyone (`.claude/ux-web/DECISIONS.md:10`), so nobody takes the reminders the calendar card now describes for a Pro feature. The answer (`faq.items[1].answer` at `src/content/site/en.ts:94`, `es.ts:94`, `ca.ts:100`) becomes exactly: EN `Yes. You get 10 free dictations a month, and one dictation can hold several tasks. When they’re used up, you keep adding tasks with a short form, with no limit, until they come back the next month. Reminders are free too, even the ones that come more and more often as the day gets closer. TaskFlow Pro, a monthly subscription that renews until you cancel it in Google Play, gives you unlimited dictation and file space (with a safety limit of 50 dictations a day). It also turns sentences you type into tasks, and lets you ask for reminders in your own words. Its price isn’t set yet.` / ES `Sí. Tienes 10 dictados gratis al mes, y en un dictado caben varias tareas. Cuando se acaban, sigues añadiendo tareas con un formulario sencillo, sin límite, hasta que vuelven el mes siguiente. Los recordatorios también son gratis, incluso los que llegan cada vez más a menudo según se acerca el día. TaskFlow Pro, una suscripción mensual que se renueva hasta que la cancelas en Google Play, te da dictado y espacio para archivos ilimitados (con un límite de seguridad de 50 dictados al día). Además, convierte en tareas las frases que escribes y te deja pedir los recordatorios con tus palabras. Su precio aún no está decidido.` / CA `Sí. Tens 10 dictats gratuïts al mes, i en un dictat hi caben diverses tasques. Quan s’acaben, continues afegint tasques amb un formulari senzill, sense límit, fins que tornen el mes següent. Els recordatoris també són gratuïts, fins i tot els que arriben cada cop més sovint a mesura que s’acosta el dia. TaskFlow Pro, una subscripció mensual que es renova fins que la cancel·les a Google Play, et dona dictat i espai per a fitxers il·limitats (amb un límit de seguretat de 50 dictats al dia). A més, converteix en tasques les frases que escrius i et deixa demanar els recordatoris amb les teves paraules. El preu encara no està decidit.`

That is three changes, and nothing else in the answer moves. (1) A new sentence after ‘…until they come back the next month.’: EN `Reminders are free too, even the ones that come more and more often as the day gets closer.` / ES `Los recordatorios también son gratis, incluso los que llegan cada vez más a menudo según se acerca el día.` / CA `Els recordatoris també són gratuïts, fins i tot els que arriben cada cop més sovint a mesura que s’acosta el dia.` (2) The Pro sentence now ends at WD14's parenthesis, which still comes right after ‘unlimited dictation and file space’ / «dictado y espacio para archivos ilimitados» / «dictat i espai per a fitxers il·limitats». (3) Its last clause, ‘and also turns sentences you type into tasks’ / «y además convierte en tareas las frases que escribes» / «i a més converteix en tasques les frases que escrius», becomes a sentence of its own and gains the new Pro item: EN `It also turns sentences you type into tasks, and lets you ask for reminders in your own words.` / ES `Además, convierte en tareas las frases que escribes y te deja pedir los recordatorios con tus palabras.` / CA `A més, converteix en tasques les frases que escrius i et deixa demanar els recordatoris amb les teves paraules.` The price sentence still ends the answer.

Why these words. ‘In your own words’ / «con tus palabras» / «amb les teves paraules» is already the voice answer's phrase. It says what the feature does without naming the sheet's row («A tu manera» / ‘Your way’ / «A la teva manera»), which the site mustn't quote while the app's D1–D7 round runs; the owner adds the name to the Pro screen in RevenueCat himself (D7). The free sentence repeats the calendar card's words, so the two read as one feature. Splitting the Pro sentence keeps every sentence shorter than today's longest: the Pro sentence goes from 38 words to 30 in English (42 → 33 in Spanish, 44 → 34 in Catalan), and the new sentences are 17 to 21 words. The answer grows from 80 words to 108 in English (107 in Spanish, 112 in Catalan), which is what the owner asked for. ‘Reminders are free too’ is true of every reminder: the single reminder and the three strengths cost nothing. A free account can also say a rhythm while dictating, at the cost of a dictation (`REMINDER_PLANS.md:12`). The answer needn't say so, and Pro's clause stays true: the app's own Pro screen says the same (`billingReasonReminderPlans`, ‘With Pro, ask for reminders in your own words:’). Privacy §4 already covers those words going to Google (‘With Pro, words you type for the AI are sent the same way. Without Pro, the task form never sends anything to the AI.’, WP58), so no legal page changes.

Update the copy these changes pin, exactly, and nothing else in those files. In `tests/support/ux-web-copy.ts`: `:48-50` (`FEATURES.cards[0].body`, read by ‘each feature card says what the app does’, `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts:59`) and `:134-136` (`FAQ_FIRST[1].answer`, read by `:189`); the comment at `:112-113` may add `WP60 adds the free reminders and Pro's reminders in your own words, and ends the Pro sentence after that clause.` In `tests/ux-web-features.spec.ts`: `CALENDAR_BODY` (`:662-666`), with its comment at `:656`, which becomes `// WP53, WP59, WP60: the calendar card's paragraph, without ‘the first time you add one’ or ‘it asks you once’, and with reminders that come more and more often.`; the title of `:759`, which becomes `WEB-1003, WEB-1102, WEB-1103: the calendar card's paragraph says TaskFlow can remind you of tasks with a date, more and more often as the day gets closer, with no ‘the first time you add one’ and no ‘it asks you once’ (${theme})`; and WP59's test at `:955-970`, which pins the old ending. Rename it `WEB-1102, WEB-1103: the calendar card's paragraph ends with reminders that come more and more often as the day gets closer, with no colon, in every language`, set `ENDS` to the three new last sentences, keep the no-colon check, and change the English word count at `:968` from 27 to 36. Leave `OLD_CALENDAR`, `OLD_ASKS_ONCE` and every other test to web-ux-tester.

decisions.question: Say on the calendar card that TaskFlow's reminders can come more and more often as a task's day gets closer?
decisions.recommendation: Plan 1: yes, on the card only, in review F's words.
decisions.answer: The calendar card's reminder sentence says that reminders can come more often as a task's day gets closer (`.claude/ux-web/DECISIONS.md:9`). Built by WP60 (WEB-1103) in review F's words.

decisions.question: Add ‘reminders in your own words’ (Pro: a rhythm you type or say, read by Google's AI) to the Pro list in the FAQ's ‘Is TaskFlow free?’ answer?
decisions.recommendation: Plan 1: not now; revisit when Pro's price is set, or when the app's Pro screen names it.
decisions.answer: «Let's add that your way in [the FAQ]»: reminders asked for in your own words join the Pro list next to unlimited dictation and file space, and the free answer says the until-the-day reminders are for everyone (`.claude/ux-web/DECISIONS.md:10`). Built by WP60 (WEB-1104).
